# Standard library: files, flags, time, math and tests

<!-- Generated by skill/plutonium/tools/genstdlib from lib/pluto. Do not edit; regenerate. -->

Files and processes, command-line flags, time, math, bit tricks, the test package and the profiler.

Listing of the hosted build (linux, amd64): every exported name, one line each, with the
ownership kind of each type (`value`, `view`, `owner (moves)`, `counted`; see section 8.7). Methods are
indented under their type. For the full comment of a name run `pluto doc pluto/strings Cut` or
`pluto doc pluto/vec Vec.Push`. `(*T)` is a pointer receiver (borrows); `(T)` on an owner type
consumes the receiver.

Packages in this file: `pluto/os`, `pluto/os/exec`, `pluto/path/filepath`, `pluto/flag`, `pluto/time`, `pluto/math`, `pluto/bits`, `pluto/cmp`, `pluto/testing`, `pluto/prof`.

```
type T struct { _ unexported }  [view]
  // T is the state of one test or subtest.
  func (*T) Error(args ...any)  // promoted
  func (*T) Errorf(format string, args ...any)  // promoted
  func (*T) Fail()  // promoted
  func (*T) FailNow()  // promoted
  func (*T) Failed() bool  // promoted
  func (*T) Fatal(args ...any)  // promoted
  func (*T) Fatalf(format string, args ...any)  // promoted
  func (*T) Helper()  // promoted
  func (*T) Log(args ...any)  // promoted
  func (*T) Logf(format string, args ...any)  // promoted
  func (*T) Name() string  // promoted
  func (t *T) Run(name string, f func(t *T)) bool
  func (*T) Skip(args ...any)  // promoted
  func (*T) SkipNow()  // promoted
  func (*T) Skipf(format string, args ...any)  // promoted
  func (*T) Skipped() bool  // promoted
```

## pluto/prof

Package prof profiles a running program: where it spends CPU time, and where it allocates memory. It writes profiles in the format of pprof (github.com/google/pprof), uncompressed, so that "go tool pprof" and the other pprof tools read them.

```
func StartAllocProfile(rate int) error
func StartCPUProfile() error
func StopAllocProfile(name string) error
func StopCPUProfile(name string) error
```
